statement.p: Find the point of intersection, P, of the lines \mathbf{r}_1 and \mathbf{r}_2.

static.solution:
t_1 and t_2 such that \mathbf{r}_1(t_1) = \mathbf{r}_2(t_2).
That is
\left\lt 5.5,17.5,0\right> + t_1 \left\lt 1,3,2\right> = \left\lt 1,7,-4\right> + t_2 \left\lt -2,-3,1\right>.
This is equivalent to the three equations for the components:
x = 5.5 + 1 t_1 = 1 - 2 t_2,
y = 17.5 + 3 t_1 = 7 - 3 t_2,
z = 0 + 2 t_1 = -4 + 1 t_2.
Solving the first two equations for t_1 and t_2 in turn yields
t_1 = -2.5 and t_2 = -1
Now, substituting these values into the third equation yields
0 - 2.5 * 2 = -4 - 1 * 1
-5 = -5
Since this does indeed come out equal, the lines intersect at the point
\left\lt 5.5,17.5,0\right> - 2.5 * \left\lt 1,3,2\right> = \left\lt 3,10,-5\right>
Note: If the third equation could not be reconciled, that would mean that the lines do not intersect.
